summary.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning

setting_and_object.category: Benchmark / Dataset + evaluation protocol (closed-loop suite with training data, verifiable scorers, and RL)

details: Native visual reasoning (solving problems by generating/updating visual states as the reasoning substrate) lacks scalable trainable tasks, reliable verifiable feedback, and controlled cross-modality comparison.
Prevalent VLM-as-a-judge evaluation is inaccurate, costly, and non-reproducible for tasks needing exact counts, spatial relations, and temporal consistency.

VBVR-Pro: a closed-loop suite of 300 procedurally generated visual reasoning tasks, each a parameterized generator plus programmatic solver that renders the SAME instance into aligned video, image (last-/key-/multi-frame), and interleaved text-image modalities.

Per-task deterministic verifiable reward scorers that extract semantic entities (color/shape/position/count via HSV segmentation, contours, OCR, tracking) and apply weighted or multiplicative task-specific checks, usable both as evaluation metric and as RL reward.
Enables three uses: scalable training curriculum, human-aligned verifiable evaluation, and modality-controlled mechanism study of image vs. video vs. interleaved generation.
300 generators (150 reworked from VBVR, 150 newly designed) organized by five cognitive faculties: perception, spatiality, transformation, abstraction, knowledge; multi-label allowed.

250 tasks x 5,000 instances = 1.25M training instances; 50 held-out OOD tasks; VBVR-Pro-Bench = 50 in-domain + 50 OOD tasks with per-task verifiable scorers; separate 50K RL subset over 50 in-domain tasks.

Interleaved textual reasoning steps generated by Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview using one hand-designed prompt per task; metadata (seed, spec, solution, attributes) recorded for verification and de-duplication.

Nine open-source generators fine-tuned on VBVR-Pro-Dataset for one epoch at 512x512: image (BAGEL-7B-MoT, Qwen-Image-Edit, FLUX.2-dev), interleaved (ThinkMorph-7B, SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT), video (Wan2.2-I2V-A14B, Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, Wan2.1-I2V-14B-720P, LTX-2.3-I2AV).

Rank-32 LoRA for all video models and >10B image/interleaved models; full fine-tuning for smaller ones; video at 16 fps; over 30 proprietary and open models benchmarked (e.g., Seedance 2.0, GPT-Image-2).
Arena-style human study: 100 tasks x 1 instance, 8 video models, all 28 model pairs, 10 annotators per pair rating each video on a 4-level rubric mapped to win/tie-above-failure/tie-at-failure/loss.

Compared against VLM judges (GPT-5.5, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Qwen3.7-plus, InternVL3.5-38B, GLM-4.6V-Flash, Gemma4-31B, Qwen3.6-27B) on per-vote agreement, model-level rank correlation, cost per evaluation, and re-run reproducibility.

All RL starts from VBVR-Pro-Wan2.2-TI2V-5B on the same 50K in-domain subset; compares SFT vs. RLVLM (Qwen3.6-27B judge reward) vs. RLVR (verifiable scorer reward) with identical algorithm/hyperparameters.

Group-relative policy optimization with Coefficients-Preserving Sampling (CPS) instead of Flow-SDE for exploration; 30 denoising steps, 32 prompts x 32 trajectories, lr 5e-6, eta=0.7, no KL; one-step-delayed rollout pipeline on 128 H800 GPUs.
Interleaved training ablations: full trajectory vs. single-image (remove intermediate visual states) vs. placeholder text (remove textual semantics).
Nine inference-time interventions on inputs (rephrase, strip task semantics, remove image, geometric counterfactuals) and on intermediate states (remove/contradict text, remove/noise image).

Nearest-neighbor retrieval against training set with CLIP, DINOv2, and BGE text embeddings; Chain-of-Step visualization by decoding intermediate diffusion latents; transfer to seven external benchmarks (RISE-Video, V-ReasonBench, RULER-Bench, MME-CoF-Pro, VideoThinkBench, BabyVision, IntelligentVBench).

key_findings.finding: Rule-based verifiable scorers align with human judgment better than strong VLM judges while being far cheaper and fully deterministic.
key_findings.evidence: Per-vote agreement exceeds 0.60 versus 0.54 for GPT-5.5 and 0.52 for Gemini-3.1-Pro, reaching about 78% of the 0.77 human ceiling; model-level Spearman rho of 0.95 in-domain and 1.00 OOD (up from 0.93 with the earlier VBVR scorer); repeated runs change scores for 0% of cases versus 54.6-92.8% for VLM judges even at temperature 0.

key_findings.finding: Verifiable rewards outperform VLM-judge rewards and SFT for multi-task RL, including on tasks never seen during RL.
key_findings.evidence: From the same VBVR-Pro-Wan2.2-TI2V-5B initialization and data, RLVR reaches 0.548 overall versus 0.508 (RLVLM) and 0.503 (SFT), with OOD 0.377 vs 0.345 vs 0.328; RLVR improves steadily over training while RLVLM stagnates and drops around steps 400-500 due to unpenalized background-color degradation; RLVR also gives 1.63x training throughput (5.1 vs 8.3 days for 2,200 steps on 128 H800s).

key_findings.finding: Intermediate visual states, not linguistic chains of thought, are the critical substrate for native visual reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: Compressing trajectories to a single image drops overall score by 0.024 (ThinkMorph) and 0.111 (SenseNova-U1), while replacing reasoning text with uninformative placeholders has much smaller effect; at inference, removing or noising the intermediate image degrades performance substantially more than removing or contradicting intermediate text.

key_findings.finding: Training on the 300-task suite transfers to held-out tasks and external real-world benchmarks rather than fitting instruction templates.
key_findings.evidence: All nine fine-tuned models improve, averaging +0.290 overall (+0.401 in-domain, +0.179 OOD); VBVR-Pro-Wan2.2-I2V-A14B gains up to 20 points across seven external benchmarks including embodied reasoning in MME-CoF-Pro; nearest-neighbor retrieval finds no visually similar training instances, rephrasing the prompt leaves performance unchanged while removing the image collapses it to 0.064, and geometric counterfactuals still yield correct trajectories.

key_findings.finding: Video generation is best for tasks requiring state-transition tracking, while interleaved generation is a compute-efficient near-equal alternative and single-image generation is clearly weakest.
key_findings.evidence: After training, VBVR-Pro-SenseNova-U1 matches VBVR-Pro-Wan2.2-I2V-A14B on many in-domain tasks at lower inference cost, but video leads on in-domain transformation tasks and across OOD categories; qualitative cases show video succeeding on shortest-path manipulation and 180-degree block rotation where interleaved and image models fail.
